paragraphs.text: Therefore we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things that were heard, lest haply we drift away [from them].
paragraphs.original: Διὰ τοῦτο δεῖ περισσοτέρως προσέχειν ἡμᾶς τοῖς ἀκουσθεῖσιν, μήποτε παραρυῶμεν.
paragraphs.translit: Dia touto dei perissoterōs prosechein hēmas tois akoustheisin, mēpote pararyōmen.

paragraphs.text: For if the word spoken through angels proved stedfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense of reward;
paragraphs.original: εἰ γὰρ ὁ διʼ ἀγγέλων λαληθεὶς λόγος ἐγένετο βέβαιος, καὶ πᾶσα παράβασις καὶ παρακοὴ ἔλαβεν ἔνδικον μισθαποδοσίαν,
paragraphs.translit: ei gar ho diʼ angelōn lalētheis logos egeneto bebaios, kai pasa parabasis kai parakoē elaben endikon misthapodosian,

paragraphs.text: how shall we escape, if we neglect so great a salvation? which having at the first been spoken through the Lord, was confirmed unto us by them that heard;
paragraphs.original: πῶς ἡμεῖς ἐκφευξόμεθα τηλικαύτης ἀμελήσαντες σωτηρίας, ἥτις, ἀρχὴν λαβοῦσα λαλεῖσθαι διὰ τοῦ κυρίου, ὑπὸ τῶν ἀκουσάντων εἰς ἡμᾶς ἐβεβαιώθη,
paragraphs.translit: pōs hēmeis ekpheuxometha tēlikautēs amelēsantes sōtērias, hētis, archēn labousa laleisthai dia tou kyriou, hypo tōn akousantōn eis hēmas ebebaiōthē,

paragraphs.text: God also bearing witness with them, both by signs and wonders, and by manifold powers, and by gifts of the Holy Spirit, according to his own will.
paragraphs.original: συνεπιμαρτυροῦντος τοῦ θεοῦ σημείοις τε καὶ τέρασιν καὶ ποικίλαις δυνάμεσιν καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου μερισμοῖς κατὰ τὴν αὐτοῦ θέλησιν;
paragraphs.translit: synepimartyrountos tou theou sēmeiois te kai terasin kai poikilais dynamesin kai pneumatos hagiou merismois kata tēn autou thelēsin;

paragraphs.text: For not unto angels did he subject the world to come, whereof we speak.
paragraphs.original: Οὐ γὰρ ἀγγέλοις ὑπέταξεν τὴν οἰκουμένην τὴν μέλλουσαν, περὶ ἧς λαλοῦμεν·
paragraphs.translit: Ou gar angelois hypetaxen tēn oikoumenēn tēn mellousan, peri hēs laloumen·

paragraphs.text: But one hath somewhere testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? Or the son of man, that thou visitest him?
paragraphs.original: διεμαρτύρατο δέ πού τις λέγων· Τί ἐστιν ἄνθρωπος ὅτι μιμνῄσκῃ αὐτοῦ, ἢ υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου ὅτι ἐπισκέπτῃ αὐτόν;
paragraphs.translit: diemartyrato de pou tis legōn· Ti estin anthrōpos hoti mimnēskē autou, ē hyios anthrōpou hoti episkeptē auton;

paragraphs.text: Thou madest him a little lower than the angels; Thou crownedst him with glory and honor, And didst set him over the works of thy hands:
paragraphs.original: ἠλάττωσας αὐτὸν βραχύ τι παρʼ ἀγγέλους, δόξῃ καὶ τιμῇ ἐστεφάνωσας αὐτόν,
paragraphs.translit: ēlattōsas auton brachy ti parʼ angelous, doxē kai timē estephanōsas auton,

paragraphs.text: Thou didst put all things in subjection under his feet.     For in that he subjected all things unto him, he left nothing that is not subject to him. But now we see not yet all things subjected to him.
paragraphs.original: πάντα ὑπέταξας ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ· ἐν τῷ γὰρ ὑποτάξαι τὰ πάντα οὐδὲν ἀφῆκεν αὐτῷ ἀνυπότακτον. νῦν δὲ οὔπω ὁρῶμεν αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα ὑποτεταγμένα·
paragraphs.translit: panta hypetaxas hypokatō tōn podōn autou· en tō gar hypotaxai ta panta ouden aphēken autō anypotakton. nyn de oupō horōmen autō ta panta hypotetagmena·

paragraphs.text: But we behold him who hath been made a little lower than the angels, [even] Jesus, because of the suffering of death crowned with glory and honor, that by the grace of God he should taste of death for every [man].
paragraphs.original: τὸν δὲ βραχύ τι παρʼ ἀγγέλους ἠλαττωμένον βλέπομεν Ἰησοῦν διὰ τὸ πάθημα τοῦ θανάτου δόξῃ καὶ τιμῇ ἐστεφανωμένον, ὅπως χωρὶς θεοῦ ὑπὲρ παντὸς γεύσηται θανάτου.
paragraphs.translit: ton de brachy ti parʼ angelous ēlattōmenon blepomen Iēsoun dia to pathēma tou thanatou doxē kai timē estephanōmenon, hopōs chōris theou hyper pantos geusētai thanatou.

paragraphs.text: For it became him, for whom are all things, and through whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the author of their salvation perfect through sufferings.
paragraphs.original: Ἔπρεπεν γὰρ αὐτῷ, διʼ ὃν τὰ πάντα καὶ διʼ οὗ τὰ πάντα, πολλοὺς υἱοὺς εἰς δόξαν ἀγαγόντα τὸν ἀρχηγὸν τῆς σωτηρίας αὐτῶν διὰ παθημάτων τελειῶσαι.
paragraphs.translit: Eprepen gar autō, diʼ hon ta panta kai diʼ hou ta panta, pollous hyious eis doxan agagonta ton archēgon tēs sōtērias autōn dia pathēmatōn teleiōsai.

paragraphs.text: For both he that sanctifieth and they that are sanctified are all of one: for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren,
paragraphs.original: ὅ τε γὰρ ἁγιάζων καὶ οἱ ἁγιαζόμενοι ἐξ ἑνὸς πάντες· διʼ ἣν αἰτίαν οὐκ ἐπαισχύνεται ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοὺς καλεῖν,
paragraphs.translit: ho te gar hagiazōn kai hoi hagiazomenoi ex henos pantes· diʼ hēn aitian ouk epaischynetai adelphous autous kalein,

paragraphs.text: saying, I will declare thy name unto my brethren, In the midst of the congregation will I sing thy praise.
paragraphs.original: λέγων· Ἀπαγγελῶ τὸ ὄνομά σου τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς μου, ἐν μέσῳ ἐκκλησίας ὑμνήσω σε·
paragraphs.translit: legōn· Apangelō to onoma sou tois adelphois mou, en mesō ekklēsias hymnēsō se·

paragraphs.text: And again, I will put my trust in him. And again, Behold, I and the children whom God hath given me.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πάλιν· Ἐγὼ ἔσομαι πεποιθὼς ἐπʼ αὐτῷ· καὶ πάλιν· Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ καὶ τὰ παιδία ἅ μοι ἔδωκεν ὁ θεός.
paragraphs.translit: kai palin· Egō esomai pepoithōs epʼ autō· kai palin· Idou egō kai ta paidia ha moi edōken ho theos.

paragraphs.text: Since then the children are sharers in flesh and blood, he also himself in like manner partook of the same; that through death he might bring to nought him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;
paragraphs.original: Ἐπεὶ οὖν τὰ παιδία κεκοινώνηκεν αἵματος καὶ σαρκός, καὶ αὐτὸς παραπλησίως μετέσχεν τῶν αὐτῶν, ἵνα διὰ τοῦ θανάτου καταργήσῃ τὸν τὸ κράτος ἔχοντα τοῦ θανάτου, τοῦτʼ ἔστι τὸν διάβολον,
paragraphs.translit: Epei oun ta paidia kekoinōnēken haimatos kai sarkos, kai autos paraplēsiōs meteschen tōn autōn, hina dia tou thanatou katargēsē ton to kratos echonta tou thanatou, toutʼ esti ton diabolon,

paragraphs.text: and might deliver all them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπαλλάξῃ τούτους, ὅσοι φόβῳ θανάτου διὰ παντὸς τοῦ ζῆν ἔνοχοι ἦσαν δουλείας.
paragraphs.translit: kai apallaxē toutous, hosoi phobō thanatou dia pantos tou zēn enochoi ēsan douleias.

paragraphs.text: For verily not to angels doth he give help, but he giveth help to the seed of Abraham.
paragraphs.original: οὐ γὰρ δήπου ἀγγέλων ἐπιλαμβάνεται, ἀλλὰ σπέρματος Ἀβραὰμ ἐπιλαμβάνεται.
paragraphs.translit: ou gar dēpou angelōn epilambanetai, alla spermatos Abraam epilambanetai.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore it behooved him in all things to be made like unto his brethren, that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make propitiation for the sins of the people.
paragraphs.original: ὅθεν ὤφειλεν κατὰ πάντα τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ὁμοιωθῆναι, ἵνα ἐλεήμων γένηται καὶ πιστὸς ἀρχιερεὺς τὰ πρὸς τὸν θεόν, εἰς τὸ ἱλάσκεσθαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ λαοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: hothen ōpheilen kata panta tois adelphois homoiōthēnai, hina eleēmōn genētai kai pistos archiereus ta pros ton theon, eis to hilaskesthai tas hamartias tou laou·

paragraphs.text: For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succor them that are tempted.
paragraphs.original: ἐν ᾧ γὰρ πέπονθεν αὐτὸς πειρασθείς, δύναται τοῖς πειραζομένοις βοηθῆσαι.
paragraphs.translit: en hō gar peponthen autos peirastheis, dynatai tois peirazomenois boēthēsai.
